title: UTF-8 encoding of Hello算法
summary: Compare single-byte and three-byte encodings across seven characters, identifying leading bytes and continuation bytes.
context: The input string is Hello算法 without spaces. The figure writes the code points of these 7 characters in 16 bits because all of them fall within U+FFFF; the full Unicode code point range extends up to U+10FFFF and requires 21 bits, so this example should not be generalized to mean that every code point fits in 16 bits.

frames.title: UTF-8 encoding of Hello算法
frames.explanation: Each English character uses the single-byte template 0xxxxxxx, placing its code point in the lower 7 bits. Both "算" and "法" use the three-byte template 1110xxxx 10xxxxxx 10xxxxxx: the leading byte starts with prefix 1110, where the 0 after the three 1s is also part of the prefix, and each of the two continuation bytes starts with 10. The remaining 4 + 6 + 6 payload bits hold the code point in order: "算" splits into 0111, 101110, and 010111, while "法" splits into 0110, 110011, and 010101.

tables.caption: Per-character code points and UTF-8 bytes

result: These bit prefixes distinguish single-byte characters, multi-byte leading bytes, and continuation bytes. In this example, the five English characters take 1 byte each and the two Chinese characters take 3 bytes each, for a total of 5 × 1 + 2 × 3 = 11 bytes.
